newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Toyota Indonesia unit to launch low-price vehicles.
newsitem.headline: Toyota Indonesia unit to launch low-price vehicles.

text.p: Indonesia' largest car assembler PT Toyota Astra Motor, a unit of PT Astra International , is likely to launch two new models of its popular Kijang recreational vehicle, industry sources said.

Sources said Toyota Astra Motor (TAM), a joint venture of Astra International and Toyota Motor Corp of Japan, will launch new versions of Kijang in order to maintain its leading position in the market.
One model will be petrol-fuelled while the other will run on diesel, they said.
"I think their strategy is to compete with cheap sedans which will be available this year because they are in the same price range of 40 to 50 million rupiah," said one source.

PT Timor Putra Nasional, a company controlled by President Suharto's youngest son, has launched 1500 cc sedans at a price of about 35 million rupiah after receiving tax breaks under the controversial national car policy.
Under the policy, the company has to have local content of 60 percent in its cars within three years of starting operations.
Astra officials said their company is also targeting local content of 60 percent in all the cars it assembles to qualify for tax breaks.

On Friday, Bisnis Indonesia daily quoted Astra International president director Theodore P. Rachmat saying that Toyota Motor Corp will use Indonesia as a production base for a new series called "Asia Family Car".
"The 1,500 cc sedan will be fully manufactured here and contain 40 percent local components," Rachmat was quoted as saying. The daily did not give details of pricing.
"By the year 2000, we expect to export about 75,000 to 100,000 assembled car every year," he added.
